steps.text: Rhodes Island Convalescent Garden
10:00 A.M. \ Sunny, clear

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Podenco.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Oh, Miss Lena, you're here.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Look at the golden chrysanthemums planter over that way. It's long past their forty-day flowering period, but they still aren't wilting.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: And look at these yarny velvets. One of the yarn balls grew a layer more than usual, and the layers are all much more distinct too.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Making the right changes to a plants' nutrient intake can prolong or shorten their flowering seasons. Weren't you trying to tweak the formula of your nutrient solution?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Um, do you think you could you invite the Doctor here this weekend? They weren't here last time we did the flower display, and they've regretted missing it all this time.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Um, what's wrong?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Podenco, we might need to... get rid of these flowers.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Medical's taken on several new research projects recently, and they'll need us to provide specimen samples in bulk. Here's the list—I've already been over it with Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: There are some varieties we've never raised before, and some with extremely long life cycles. We'll be in trouble unless we start work as soon as we can.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: But the Convalescent Garden only has so much room.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Will we have to... pluck them all?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: We won't need to go that far. As long as we dedicate some space to cultivation, we'll be fine.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Can I move them to my own dorm then?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: With this many flowers, even ten dormitories wouldn't be enough.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Didn't you send Engineering an application to expand the Garden before?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: That still hasn't been approved. They're busy with other refurbishment and maintenance. We'll just have to do something about the flowers near the end of their cycle, along with a few others.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (That's still a lot, though.)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (These yarny velvets and golden chrysanthemums...)

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Podenco?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I'm sorry. I know you've been taking care of them for so long.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: But the Convalescent Garden isn't an ordinary garden.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: It's a 'supplier' for Medical, as well as an 'operating room' for aromatherapy. And it belongs to Rhodes Island, before anything else.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: We cultivate all these plants both because pretty flowers can uplift spirits, and because we hope to make use of them to help everyone in the truest sense.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Oh, I know that much, Miss Lena. I've had to pluck pretty flowers all the time back home, too.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: ...You've never talked about your home before.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mostly because there's not much to say. Do you still remember the nomadic city where we met for the first time?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: It was a tiny, faraway place, but it took me a whole month to get there from home.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I think you used to live in a plateau settlement, on the Bolívarian border?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm-hm. We were living off the land ever since I can remember, not that we had a choice. People barely ever wanted to see what it was like outside. They said it was a mess out there.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: We planted so many crops. At first it was millet, then at some point the adults pulled all the millet out while it was still sprouts, and switched to coffee beans.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: 'Bolívarian coffee.' Not just any bean can lay claim to a whole country's name. The largest cities sell it as a popular souvenir, and the demand is endless both domestic and abroad.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: And so, though masses of its people go hungry, Bolívar still has all sorts of regional policies in place to encourage the growing of cash crops.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: It was completely new to us, so we didn't have experience growing it. And the soil is hard in the plateau, and the drainage is poor. It wasn't good for growing coffee at all.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: All the land in our village was used to plant it, but the harvests were miserable, the beans didn't meet the standard, and the reward wasn't enough to trade for the grains we used to grow.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Watch out, Podenco.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Keep walking and you would've kicked the boronias over.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Oh, sorry, sorry.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (But we're going to have to get rid of them anyway.)

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Later on, we planted a few other cash crops, too, which went about as well as the coffee, until finally we went back to millet.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: But that didn't work either. Every harvest season, we'd get people coming to levy our grains. I couldn't tell you if they were from the Singas dynasty, the Coalition, or True Bolívarians.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Or maybe they were just a bunch of awful people who wandered around the border plateau.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: We could escape Catastrophe, but we couldn't escape them. Our only real option was to develop the wild land and plant more grains.

a.text: But whether we were planting coffee beans or millet, we always saw wild flowers in the soil.
Red ones, yellow ones, light pink ones... I didn't know their names at the time.
They grew all around the fields. They were really beautiful, and they smelled pretty too.
Whenever it was time to water, I'd sprinkle a little at their roots, and occasionally I'd transplant a few of them into our house's nursery.
My dad would pluck any left in the ground. So would the others in the village. Afterwards, so would I.
And because we didn't have much fertilizer to spare for them, the ones in the nursery didn't live long either.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Compared to the coffee beans or the millet, the flowers were nothing more than weeds.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I understand, Podenco.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: But what about after you plucked those flowers?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: After?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: That's right. What did you do with them after?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: There's still a bit more to what I said earlier. We cultivate so many plants, and we do grow pretty flowers to uplift spirits, but also in hopes of making use of them to help everyone in the truest sense.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: But not all plants have medicinal value, or are able to cure the sick. The existence of some flowers is purely to cheer us up.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: But it's not as if flowers grow on branches just to make us happy.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: For them, going from budding to blooming to wilting is nothing more than a natural cycle.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: There's a saying in Minos: 'When a flower blooms on a branch, it is embracing the whole land.'

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: And a Yanese operator once told me they have a poem that goes something like 'petals fall upon the ground, come with the soil, their fragrance still as old'... I can't remember the original exactly.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: In other words, the flowering season comes to a close, but the flowers' lives aren't over yet.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Back home... I'd try air-drying the flowers sometimes, so I could put them up for a while more.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Is that so.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Podenco, I'll help however I can. Let's sort out these flowers together.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Umm... no, it's okay, I want to figure this out by myself.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: The golden chrysanthemums, and yarny velvets, and boronias... I've been looking after all these plants on the south end this whole time.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: All I did for the wild flowers back home was pick them. But now... I think you just helped me figure a lot of things out, Miss Lena.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: ...Alright then. For now, here's the Medical Department's list of new plants. Don't lose it.
Rhodes Island Convalescent Garden
The yarny velvets have been air-drying naturally for two days. I think they should be good now.
First, trim away the stems and leaves that are already damaged.
Then apply the desiccant. It's the trickiest but the most important step. Too thin a coating and it won't preserve for long, too thick and it'll completely block their scent.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Once the desiccant is on, stand them in fine sand for... ten minutes—no, fifteen.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (I tried a whole parade of chemicals to find the right ingredient blend for this desiccant. It should work great.)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (Dried flowers don't last very long if you just rely on air-drying—they wither before you know it. Just like the ones from back then...)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (Oh, it would've been so nice to have all this stuff back home.)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Phew—now the desiccant just needs to completely absorb, and it's done.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Podenco?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Miss Lena! What are you doing here?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I'm preparing what I need for aromatherapy. Nyctomaluses only bloom in the dead of morning, and I'm here to collect their pollen.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Oh! Is it that late already...?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Yarny velvets have quite large flowers, and there's a rich sense of layering between their petals. There's more ornamental value in drying them than you'd think.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: You've treated so many velvets, it's become like a little dried flower shop in here.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Oh, what's this?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Floral teabags.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Boronia petals?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm-hm! I saw Rosa drinking tea and the idea just came to me. I've already tried it. The aroma's very strong, plus a tiny bit sweet, and it's easier to brew than tea leaves.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Have you been up since yesterday making all this?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Oh, you must be so tired, Podenco.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: But I'm not done... There are still the couple dozen pots of chrysanthemums left. Their aroma's very mild. It could easily be lost when using special treatments.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (But I'm sure I can think of something else. I can't just throw them away. Mm-hm.)

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Say, why don't you let me help after all?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: It's okay. You assigned me this task, so it's my job now. I'll be sure to see it through.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Mm. Alright.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I remember you telling me the same thing, the first time we met.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Oh...
Border of Bolívar, a small nomadic city
Market
3:00 P.M. \ Sunny, clear

steps.name: Farm Owner
steps.text: Make way! You've been wandering around all day now.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Excuse me, is there a botanical garden or exhibition hall here? Where can I find it? It's supposed to be full of fresh flowers, and the booklet said, um, they're in big nomadic cities...

steps.name: Farm Owner
steps.text: Yeah, in 'big' ones. Not here.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: What about flower fields, then?

steps.name: Farm Owner
steps.text: Eugh, look, I'm busy recruiting for the farm. Do your research before you go out on holiday, señorita. This is the Bolívarian border, middle of nowhere, we don't got nothing like that.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: (I'm not on holiday...)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: About the farm then—could you let me try? I've just left home, and I don't know where I'm going yet.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: My name's Podenco, and I've been helping in the fields since I was little. I'm familiar with lots of plants, and I've planted seven or eight kinds of crops before. Millet, coffee, hemp, even cocoa trees...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Nursery, irrigation and ventilation, weeding and fertilizing, grafting and transplanting, I can do it all. Trust me.

steps.name: Farm Owner
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Farm Owner
steps.text: (So she's not some well-to-do kid.)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: If you're worried about pay, I'd be fine without.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: But I'd like a tiny little plot where I can plant a few of my own flowers.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I've seen so many flowers on the way here I've never seen before, and I've collected heaps of seeds already. They'll make your farm really pretty.

steps.name: Farm Owner
steps.text: Enough, señorita, I'm busy here. There's plenty of vacant land outside the nomadic cities. You can plant flowers wherever you like.

steps.name: Farm Owner
steps.text: (Can't eat 'em, can't sell 'em either. I'd be better off paying you extra than giving you a plot for flowers... Honestly, some kid you are.)

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Well... excuse me, then. Very sorry to bother you.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Ah! Sorry, so sorry! I didn't step on you, did I?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Can I see the seeds you've collected?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Um?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Sorry, I happened to overhear you just now.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Ah. Um, yes, go ahead.
A dozen or so bags of flower seeds lie in her backpack. They're carefully sorted by size and color, and wrapped in cotton cloth cut from her clothes to let them breathe.
Lena returns the seeds to the girl before her.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Are you fond of flowers?

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm-hm. I know you can't eat them, or make money with them, but they make the earth so pretty, and they make us all happier too.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: But at the same time, they're so frail, and have trouble blooming, but then they wither so soon too, so nobody who wants to take care of them... I want to become a great gardener.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Podenco, I can provide you a garden, and you can plant whatever flowers you like there.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: What do you need me to do in return, then?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Love them always, and care for them well. That will be your job.
Podenco stares at Lena.
She gives her head a shake, seemingly lost in thought, deliberating whether she can trust this woman, but in no more than the blink of an eye, she gives a nod.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Just be a good gardener? I'll do it. I'll do everything I can to see my job through.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Alright, then. Come to me if you ever need anything.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Also, try turn in sooner than later. It's very late.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm-hm. I'll return to the dorms as soon as I put away these dried flowers.
With the velvets done standing, Podenco lays them out according to petal size.
Sheaf by sheaf, she wraps them up.
By now, the scent of desiccant has vanished. A floral perfume fills the whole room.
Three days later
Rhodes Island, Perfumer's dormitory
Lena pushes the door open.
On the table is a bouquet of dried yarny velvets, and a delicately wrapped paper bag. As soon as the fastener on the side is opened, a floral scent pervades Lena's nose.
She opens it up, and inside are boronia teabags and a box of cookies.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Ah, Miss Lena. Have you seen Podenco?

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I just got back from the Logistics Department. Is she not in the Garden? What do you need?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: She gave me a giant floral gift package, and disappeared before I could thank her.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: A floral gift package?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Flower cookies, floral tea, and dried flowers. Haha—the same one you have right there. I'm guessing everyone on the landship has one by now.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I hear she gave HR a whole stack of office paper, too, dyed in all different colors with flower extract.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I want to find her and tell her how delicious the cookies were!

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Gold chrysanthemum stamens, chopped up evenly throughout the dough. Baked with care to not only not ruin the texture, but let the fragrance make them that much more appetizing.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: (So in the end, she thought of turning the chrysanthemums into desserts. Now that was a good idea.)

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Did she ask you to help her, Blue?

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: I didn't help her with anything. I just taught her how to make cookies. All credit goes to her for figuring out how to add fresh flowers.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: All I said was that it should be fine.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Anyway, give her my thanks if you see her.

steps.name: Blue Poison
steps.text: Oh, and let me know if you ever need help at the Garden, too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Lena! Hey there, Miss In-Your-Dorm-For-Once. Anyway, this is for you.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Construction work to expand the Convalescent Garden, approved. Dr. Amiya already signed off.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We'll move some of the energy storage facilities to another part of the ship, and that should give you plenty more floorspace. We'll start the evaluation next week, and if all's good, it's hammer time.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Why so suddenly?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Is it? You've applied, like, a couple of times already.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: But you never gave it the nod...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, I was pretty tied up before.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There's been a bunch of operators requesting to expand the Garden, lately. Blue Poison, for one... Honestly, I expected her apply for more ovens.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Rhodes needs a bigger chill-out area, anyway. The gaming room and the Garden are both getting cramped. And obviously, 'let's expand the gaming room' ain't exactly an idea with legs.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh, yeah, I got an application from a Convalescent Garden op too.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It said you had to clear out a whole bunch of plants and stuff before you could cultivate what Medical needed.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It also said she was willing to make her own dorm part of the expansion, and she could move the arbors in herself for max plant care convenience.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Podenco...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Point is, we summed up our ops' views and reached this conclusion. Not to mention Medical needs more stuff by the day—expanding the Garden was always on Engineering's agenda.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Thank you, Closure.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No problemo! And I mean, who could refuse flower cookies AND flower tea that good, you know? Plus, I got a double portion!
Rhodes Island Convalescent Garden

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Summer wisteria, fire croton, hiemalgrass... mille-feuille artemesia...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Suramakula, Yamakaphala...

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Oh, Miss Lena, you're here.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I just double-checked all the species and quantities.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I've verified them myself. The labelling for all the necessary water and soil nutrient ratios is fine. This new batch of plants for Medical is settling in well.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Oh, you must be so tired, Podenco.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: You too, Miss Lena.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: We'll need to ask Procurement for two additional orders of nutrient solution.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: That reminds me, Podenco. The Engineering Department gave the expansion application the go-ahead.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Mm-hmm.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: That’s amazing!

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: We'll be twice as big. We're also planning to build two new PRTS-assisted smart greenhouses, specifically catered to the cultivation and exhibition of flowers.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: And you, Podenco, will be in charge of managing them.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Huh? Me? But I'm just an ordinary gardener.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: I know you can handle it.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: You always see the job through to the end.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: But once construction is done, other operators will be dropping by to relax day in, day out. They'll need to be welcomed properly, and we'll only grow busier with cultivation.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: I-I could move straight into the Garden, then.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Hahah. Taking care of flowers starts with taking good care of yourself. Don't mind me, now, I'll be going to see Closure about ordering that nutrient solution.

steps.name: Perfumer
steps.text: Oh, and Podenco, your cookies were delicious.

steps.name: Podenco
steps.text: Mm!
